    • getTokenSecurityScheme

      public static io.swagger.v3.oas.models.security.SecurityScheme getTokenSecurityScheme()
      Returns the security scheme describing the API token.

      The token is a static value the operator configures; it is sent in the request header named by AuthorizationFilter.TOKEN_HEADER. The deprecated query parameter fall-back is deliberately left undocumented: a machine readable spec is an invitation to use what it describes, and a token in the URL leaks into access logs, Referer headers and browser history.

      Returns:
      the api key security scheme for the token header

    • applyTokenSecurityScheme

      public static void applyTokenSecurityScheme(io.swagger.v3.oas.models.OpenAPI openApi)
      Declares the token security scheme on the given spec.

      Adds to the existing Components rather than replacing them: the reader has already filled in the model schemas at this point, and setComponents would drop them. Applied after read() for the same reason — the reader assigns the scheme map wholesale, so a pre-populated configuration could be overwritten.

      Static so the build-time spec generator applies the identical scheme, instead of a copy that could drift.

      Parameters:
      openApi - spec to declare the scheme on

    • getBearerSecurityScheme

      public static io.swagger.v3.oas.models.security.SecurityScheme getBearerSecurityScheme()
      Returns the security scheme describing the user bearer token.

      Issued by POST /auth/login, which returns the plaintext token in its response body. The endpoints requiring it also accept a logged-in browser session; that alternative is deliberately left undescribed, because a client cannot obtain a session through the API and no tooling can supply one.

      Returns:
      the http bearer security scheme

    • getTags

      public static List<io.swagger.v3.oas.models.tags.Tag> getTags()
      Returns the global tag list of the v1 API.

      Operations reference these tags by name only. Declaring them here is what gives each group in the API documentation a description, and this list's order is the order in which the groups are presented. A tag used by an operation but missing here still forms a group, just an undescribed one at the end.

      Static for the same reason as getInfo(): the build-time spec generator reuses it, so the validated spec stays identical to what this resource serves.

      Returns:
      tags of the v1 API, in presentation order
